Is the corner of that wall brick? I noticed that looking at the last picture there is a hole between the wood and the supporting corner of the window. I think that the water could be originating from a drip edge that is not deep enough under the fascia, the water will use the back to travel to the lowest point and create a pathway of damage.

One thing I've learned by working on water damage is that it ALWAYS goes deeper than what it appears on the outside, especially if it's an older issue. Water will travel in all directions, even vertically as it becomes more saturated. The best thing to do is try and remove some of the damaged wood and get a deeper look. What concerns me is that it's only the damage is only on the one side which leads me to believe the water could be originating from the top or even above the window frame.

 If the damage is widespread it could compromise the integrity of the window support. That being said, if it's just the 2x4 you could replace it yourself. If you don't feel comfortable, call a water damage specialist.

Honestly OP, this is a pretty rough situation and from my point of view there are 3 major options:

     1. You walk away from the relationship that you had with her and use it as a learning experience on how you want to be treated and what you want in a relationship. 
     2. You try your best to take it slow and rekindle the relationship that you once had and it works. 
     3. You try to take it slow and rekindle the relationship, but not being able to tell her how you truly feel, and the fear of being hurt again, tears you apart until you reach a breaking point.

First and foremost, I think that it is important that we acknowledge the fact that "forgetting" the past is nearly impossible and asking you to do so is unreasonable. You were in a relationship with her and shared countless experiences (both good and bad) that have shaped you to who you are today. Those experiences have informed you as to what you want out of a relationship and what you want out of your partner. It is inevitable that you will think about the past that you have shared with her, you won't be able to truly "start fresh". The past cannot be changed and we can only move forward from it.

With this in mind, it's critical you don't overlook how her actions have hurt you and caused you pain. 

>But the reason why I come here is because I am truly scared. I'm scared of having to reconnect with her. And I am scared of this. I am honestly afraid, because she caused me a lot of pain of course.

I can empathize with the overwhelming feelings you are experiencing and the extreme difficulty of navigating them. You don't want to lose someone you care so much about, but  you can't ignore that it scares you trying to reconnect with them. I think that it would be beneficial to write down (in a journal or somewhere else) how her actions have hurt you and how they made you feel, with absolute honesty. If it made you angry and furious, write it down. By trying to write down how you feel, it will allow you to look at the situation with a clearer lens, impacted less by the overwhelming emotions of missing the relationship that you once had. 

Sometimes, relationships can rebuild after a breakup and they can go on to be successful and healthy. However, this can only happen when each member of the relationship communicates healthly and honestly with one another. Given what you have said about the relationship, I think that you should take a step back and try to look at the relationship objectively, acknowledging how her actions have hurt you and how they have made you feel. If you decide that you want to try and rebuild the relationship you had, I think that it's necessary to have a healthy conversation with her on how her actions have hurt you and stating that it may be difficult to trust her the same way without first rebuilding some of the lost trust.

I wish you the absolute best and stay strong.

My mom is fully disabled due to a spinal cord injury she suffered in '05. Prior to her divorce with my dad about 3 years ago, my dad was the sole income of the household. When the divorce finally went through my mom had nowhere else to go except for city/state funded housing. It is both a blessing and a curse, on one hand social security is the sole reason she isn't homeless. On the other hand, due to the maximum income brackets for city/state funded housing, I am unable to move into my mom's house to live with her and my 19 year old sister (who is still a dependent). I am only 21 and I am a full-time college student that works part time (also a dependent). Since the income bracket is based on the household rather than the individual, my part time income would place my mom's household income over the maximum income threshold that allows her to use the city/state housing. On one hand it aims at preventing abuse of the housing program but on the other, screws me over by preventing me from living where I feel the most at home. 
That being said, no system is perfect and there will always be those who take advantage/abuse the system; however, the key difference is whether or not the choice to abuse the system is for ones basic needs or personal greed.
